objective: Print every guard that holds a ladder back, not only the first one the precedence order reaches
rationale: The supersonic wedge act says its ladder is not conclusive because the observed order 0.034 falls outside the credible range. Refitted 2026-08-01, that ladder fails two guards at both dimensionalities, and the one it does not name is the serious one: its increments barely shrink, minus 1.465 then minus 1.430 degrees, so the extrapolation step multiplies the finest increment by 40.7 and lands the shock angle at minus 13.73 degrees, which is not merely outside the measured range but impossible. A reader is told the order is wrong and would reasonably conclude that a better order would settle it. The uncertainty module already records every failing guard and already offers a call whose whole purpose is to say the verdict does not rest on the stated reason alone. Nothing on any surface reads it
cost_basis: measured; no compute, the guard record is already stored on every fitted ladder and the refit that found this one cost zero core minutes
expected_knowledge_gain: Every declined ladder states the full reason it was declined, so nobody spends a rung correcting a guard that was never what held it
outcome: Swept, fixed, and the item's own rationale carried a digit that is off. 25 ladders refitted through the fit and read through uq.guards_holding: the 10 curriculum studies, the 5 act ladders at the precision the acts themselves fit, 8 three rung windows over the two TMR cases, and the 2 windows of the Ahmed constant ratio ladder. Every curriculum record reproduced its own guards_failed and conclusive exactly, and uq.reportable_band returns the same answer on all 25 before and after: no verdict moved. SIX mismatches, each naming one guard while more than one binds: the supersonic wedge (order_window plus extrapolation_sanity), the NACA 0012 wing (three guards, one named), the NACA 4412 wing, the B 52, the Ahmed 35 degree body, and the Ahmed constant ratio ladder c1/c2/c3. TWO impossible extrapolations: the wedge at minus 15.753 degrees of shock angle, and the Ahmed constant ratio ladder at minus 0.084479 in drag coefficient. uq.not_conclusive_reason now names every guard the fit recorded, impossible value first, and uq.guards_holding_note says the verdict does not rest on any one of them alone; a single guard ladder reads exactly as it did, asserted in the tests. The rationale above quotes minus 13.73 degrees and 40.7, from the ladder refit, which fitted the rungs as the act's table PRINTS them at three decimals. The act fits what it solved: minus 15.753 and 42.25 at p 0.034. At an order this close to zero the extrapolation amplifies the finest increment by more than forty, so that rounding moves the answer by 2.02 degrees. Same two guards, same verdict, different digit; both readings are on the record. Cost: 0.0 core minutes, no ranks, no cells per rank, against an estimate of 1.0. Record: demo-output/website/campaign/W3_GUARD_SWEEP.md and its json companion.
